# axes.py
*`src/pySEA/rayTEM/axes.py`*

A scope's axes: named 2x2 frames, and transforms between any two of them.

**Contract:** sea-pearl's scope-map schema, SM-7
(`sea-pearl/src/pySEA/ai_wiki/sea_pearl/schema/scope-map/intents.md`), golden
cases `fixtures/axes.json` (run here by `tests/test_axes.py` when sea-pearl is
installed or checked out beside rayTEM). Change the schema first.

**Two homes, one file.** `sea_pearl/_axes_frames.py` is this file but for the
line marked `# axes-base` (its `SEASerializable` import). sea-pearl uses this
module when rayTEM is installed and its copy otherwise, so a process registers
one `Axis` and one `Axes`; sea-pearl's `test_axes_frames.py` fails when the
files differ anywhere else. **Edit both together.**

**On the twin:** `Microscope.axes` (an `Axes`, default the corrector alone);
the rays are traced in the primary axis. `Microscope.save`/`load_microscope`
carry it as `Axes.to_mapping()` in the flat JSON layout; a `.sea` stores the
objects (`axes/axes/<name>`: `matrix`, `components`, `description`; the
rotation and flip are derived, not stored). Files without axes load with the
default.

**Invariants:** `v_primary = matrix @ v_axis`; the primary's matrix is the
identity (construction refuses otherwise); `matrix(a, b) = M_b^-1 M_a`; an
unstated axis raises `KeyError` (never assumed aligned); names and component
pairs unique; `set_primary` re-expresses every matrix so no transform between
two axes changes. Nothing vendor- or EM-specific lives here (the scan/stage
"never primary" rule is the schema's, checked by sea-pearl's validator).
Dynamic rotation (an objective's Larmor rotation, scan rotation) is not
modelled: ecosystem `notes/eric/TODO_ACTIVE_2026-11-12_dynamic-axis-rotation.md`.

**Test-only gotcha:** pytest's default import mode also imports this package as
plain `rayTEM`, so a second `Axis` class is registered in a test process and a
reload may resolve to it (with a warning); compare by class name in tests.

## Axis *(class · line 103)*
One named two-dimensional frame, stated relative to the primary axis.

| Method | Kind | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `Axis.__init__(self, name, components, matrix, rotation, flipped, description)` | method | Hold a name, two component names and a matrix. |
| `Axis.components(self)` | property | Return the two component names. |
| `Axis.matrix(self)` | property | Return a copy of the 2x2 matrix to the primary axis. |
| `Axis.rotation(self)` | property | Return where this axis's first component points in the primary axis. |
| `Axis.flipped(self)` | property | Return whether this axis has the other handedness from the primary. |
| `Axis.to_primary(self, vector)` | method | Return a vector given in this axis, in the primary axis. |
| `Axis.from_primary(self, vector)` | method | Return a vector given in the primary axis, in this axis. |
